1. System Architecture & Main Workspace Tour ↑ Top

PromptVault Pro provides a unified, local-first workspace for finding, customizing, parameterizing, and executing enterprise-grade AI blueprints. All private prompt data stays entirely on your local machine.

Figure 1.1: PromptVault Pro Main Workspace, 7 Architectural Pillars & Production Prompt Card Grid Live Workspace View

Main Workspace UI Element Reference

UI Element Component Location Functional Description & Best Practice
1. 7 Domain Pillars Top pill tabs below hero header Filters your library across 7 engineering domains: Automation, Coding, Business, Marketing, Multimedia, Design, and Education. Enforces clean cognitive alignment.
2. Global Action Bar Top-right navigation bar Features quick access buttons: Manage Categories (Taxonomy), Starred (Favorites), ⇅ Data (Hub for import/export), Prompting Wiki, Help & Tour, and + New Prompt.
3. Instant Fuzzy Search Centered hero search input (⌘K) Real-time substring search across titles, descriptions, modular sections, parameter tags, authors, and hashtags with zero latency.
4. 3-Row Category Limit Category flex pill bar Limits category tags to 3 horizontal rows maximum. Additional categories are neatly bundled into a reactive + More Categories (N) pill button to prevent navigation sprawl.
5. Prompt Cards & Badges Main responsive card grid Every prompt card displays its Domain Pillar badge, Category tag, Blueprint indicator, Difficulty, dynamic variable highlights, author credit, and 1-click ⚡ Use Prompt runner trigger.

The 7 Core Architectural Domain Pillars

PromptVault Pro categorizes knowledge across 7 immutable domain disciplines:
• ⚙️ Automation & Systems: Robotic process automation, spreadsheet formulas, webhooks, API pipelines.
• 💻 Coding & Architecture: Full-stack development, refactoring, algorithms, testing, system architecture.
• 💼 Business & Strategy: Pitch decks, executive memos, competitive analysis, PRDs, strategic roadmaps.
• 📈 Marketing & SEO: High-conversion copywriting, technical SEO audits, social campaigns, email sequences.
• 🎨 Image & Multimedia: Midjourney, DALL-E, Stable Diffusion parameter specs, cinematography direction.
• ✨ UI/UX & Web Dev: Responsive component specs, design systems, accessibility (a11y), Tailwind/CSS architecture.
• 🎓 Education & Skill Building: Socratic tutoring, concept deconstruction, complex topic explanations.

2. The 3-Tier Taxonomy & Deduplication Shield ↑ Top

To prevent prompt libraries from devolving into chaotic, duplicate-ridden tag clouds, PromptVault Pro implements a rigid 3-Tier Taxonomy Tree backed by an interactive Deduplication Manager.

Figure 2.1: Taxonomy & Deduplication Manager Modal with Mode Switcher and Master Subcategory Pool Taxonomy Manager View

Taxonomy Manager UI Element Reference

UI Element Control Type Functional Description & Best Practice
1. Domain Switcher Pill tab bar across modal top Switches the active Domain Pillar (e.g. Business, Automation, Coding) to manage its categories and nested subcategories.
2. Mode Switcher [ ✏️ Edit Category ] vs [ ➕ New Category ] Toggle between modifying an existing category's subcategories and creating a new category from scratch. Prevents competing dropdown conflicts.
3. Category Dropdown Dropdown with telemetry counts Displays categories along with real-time stats: e.g. Executive Presentations (3 prompts, 9 subcats). Selecting a category instantly pulls its subcategories into view.
4. Inline Rename Button ✏️ Rename Category action button Allows renaming any category in place. Automatically executes a cascading database update across all assigned prompts so no cards are orphaned.
5. Master Subcategory Pool 100+ Interactive Chip Matrix Lists all available subcategories. Active/linked subcategories are highlighted with vibrant solid accent backgrounds (✓ Roadmaps); unlinked appear neutral (+ Name). 1-click toggles link state.
6. Active Hierarchy Accordion Collapsible domain accordion Shows the full category-to-subcategory tree for the active pillar. Each card includes a direct ✏️ Edit button and a safe delete button (prompts reassign to General).

3. Prompt Authoring, 5-Section Blueprints & Tag Autocomplete ↑ Top

PromptVault Pro supports both rapid single-text prompts and enterprise 5-section blueprints designed for high-reliability outputs.

Figure 3.1: Create / Edit Prompt Modal with Blueprint Sections, Tag Autocomplete & Originator Credits Prompt Form View

Prompt Authoring UI Element Reference

UI Element Form Section Functional Description & Best Practice
1. Title & Difficulty Header section Assign a descriptive action title and cognitive level (Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced, Expert) to guide users.
2. Multi-Category Selector Category Checkbox Grid Prompts can belong to multiple categories simultaneously. Selecting a category surfaces its contextual subcategory tags for 1-click addition.
3. 5-Section Blueprint Structured Blueprint Editor Separates Persona, Primary Objective, Dynamic Context Inputs (with {variables}), Negative Guardrails, and Output Rubric.
4. Tag Autocomplete Tag input field WordPress-style live autocomplete dropdown. As you type (e.g. s then o), shows matching tags with usage counts: 🏷️ seo (12). Keyboard navigable with arrow keys.
5. Originator Attribution Author & Author URL fields Gives visible credit on prompt cards to creators (e.g. 👤 Randy Austin - ExcelForFreelancers, 👤 Anthropic, 👤 HubSpot).
6. Safe Delete Button Bottom-left red action button Deletes the prompt with a confirmation safety modal to prevent accidental data loss.

4. Dynamic Variables & Live Multi-LLM Runner ↑ Top

Static prompts require manual find-and-replace editing. PromptVault Pro turns prompts into interactive software tools through dynamic variable parsing and upfront parameter pre-filling.

Figure 4.1: Live Variable Runner with Upfront Parameter Pre-fill, Choice Pills & Token Telemetry Live Runner View

Live Runner UI Element Reference

UI Element Runner Component Functional Description & Best Practice
1. Upfront Pre-fill Panel Top of runner modal Consolidates all prompt variables into a single upfront form. Gives users a bird's-eye view of project scope and requirements before copying.
2. Choice Toggle Pills Multiple-choice inputs Renders choices defined in {name: Opt 1 | Opt 2} as 1-click selectable pills, with a custom write-in fallback for bespoke options.
3. Live Token Telemetry Telemetry counter bar Calculates characters, words, and estimated LLM tokens (Math.ceil(characters / 4)) in real time as variables are adjusted.
4. Compile vs Template Clipboard action buttons Choose between copying the compiled prompt (with variables filled in) or copying the raw template (with placeholders intact for prompt engineers).
5. 1-Click LLM Launcher Run in LLM / Export ▾ button Opens the Multi-LLM modal to push the compiled prompt directly to your preferred AI model in a new tab.

5. ⇅ Data Hub: Ingest, Backups & Turnkey Enrichment ↑ Top

The ⇅ Data Hub provides comprehensive data sovereignty, rapid text ingestion, and multi-format backup tools.

Figure 5.1: Data Management Hub with Canvas Presets, Smart Ingest, and Multi-Format Exports Data Hub View

Data Hub UI Element Reference

UI Element Action Type Functional Description & Best Practice
1. Blank Canvas Preset 🗑️ Start from Scratch Clears all prompts to let you build your own library, while preserving all 44 categories and 7 domain pillars.
2. Starter Pack Preset ⚡ Load Starter Pack Restores the 7 flagship production blueprints across all domain disciplines.
3. Smart Ingestion Raw text-to-prompt engine Paste raw prompts with brackets ([Topic], <Audience>, {Tone}). Automatically converts them into PromptVault variables, infers titles, and adds them to your library.
4. Multi-Format Backups Export & Import actions Download portable JSON backups, download the local SQLite promptlibrary.db file, or export documentation in Markdown.
5. Turnkey LLM Prompt Copyable master prompt A pre-engineered prompt to batch-parameterize exported 0-variable prompts using ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini.

6. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) ↑ Top

Q1 Where are my prompts stored? Is my prompt data private and secure?
Your prompts are stored 100% locally on your machine inside your browser's persistent IndexedDB database. Nothing is transmitted to external servers or cloud analytics. If you run the included optional Python backend (server/server.py), prompts are saved to an offline SQLite file (promptlibrary.db).
Q2 How does the Upfront Variable Pre-fill workflow work?
Clicking "⚡ Use Prompt" opens the Upfront Variable Runner. All variables are presented upfront at the top of the modal. Seeing all variables at once gives you a bird's-eye view of your project flow. As you fill text fields or click choice pills, PromptVault Pro calculates live token consumption (Math.ceil(chars / 4)). You can copy the compiled prompt or raw template and launch any LLM with 1 click.
Q3 How do the Edit Category vs. New Category modes work in the Taxonomy Manager?
In the Taxonomy & Deduplication Manager, the top box features an explicit 2-mode switcher. ✏️ Edit Category Mode gives you a clean dropdown showing prompt and subcategory counts (e.g. Executive Presentations (3 prompts, 9 subcats)); selecting one pulls all its linked subcategories into view. ➕ New Category Mode gives you an empty, auto-focused text field to name a new category under any Domain Pillar without dropdown clutter.
Q4 How does the Master Subcategory Pool prevent duplicate tags?
The 100+ Master Subcategory Pool displays all standard tags. Subcategories that are already linked to the currently selected category are highlighted with solid vibrant accent backgrounds (✓ Roadmaps). Unlinked subcategories appear neutral (+ Name). Clicking any unlinked chip links it instantly; clicking any highlighted chip unlinks it.
Q5 What happens if I rename or delete a category? Will I lose my prompts?
No prompts are ever lost! When you click "✏️ Rename Category", PromptVault Pro automatically updates the category name across every assigned prompt in the database. If you delete a category, all associated prompts are safely moved to the General fallback category.
Q6 How does Character-by-Character Tag Autocomplete work?
When editing a prompt, typing in the Tags field triggers a WordPress-style live autocomplete dropdown. As you type each letter (e.g. s then o), existing tags refilter instantly with real-time frequency counts (🏷️ seo (12)). Use ↑ ↓ arrows and Enter to pick an existing tag, or press Enter/comma to create a new tag.
Q7 How do I delete a prompt?
Open any prompt in the editor modal and click the red "🗑️ Delete Prompt" button at the bottom left. A confirmation modal appears to prevent accidental deletions. Upon confirmation, the prompt is removed and all library indexes update immediately.
Q8 What is the difference between a Simple Prompt and a 5-Section Blueprint?
A Simple Prompt is a single text block with variables, ideal for routine tasks like emails and social posts. A 5-Section Blueprint partitions prompts into Role Persona, Core Objective, Dynamic Context Inputs, Negative Guardrails, and Output Schema/Rubric for mission-critical enterprise workflows.
Q9 How can I bulk-parameterize existing prompts that have no variables?
Open ⇅ Data -> Turnkey LLM Prompt. Export your 0-variable prompts, paste them into ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini alongside the included turnkey prompt. The LLM inserts dynamic {variables} and choice dropdowns. Re-import the resulting JSON into PromptVault Pro to enrich your prompts instantly!
Q10 Can I run PromptVault Pro completely offline?
Yes! The web application runs 100% offline via browser caching and local IndexedDB. Alternatively, you can run the included Python server (python3 server/server.py) for local SQLite persistence with zero pip dependencies.

Deduplication Shield Jump to Chapter 2 →

Domain Pillars Jump to Chapter 1 →
The 7 immutable functional disciplines organizing all knowledge: Automation, Coding, Business, Marketing, Multimedia, Design, and Education.
Fuzzy Search (⌘K) Jump to Chapter 1 →
Client-side search engine filtering titles, descriptions, sections, variables, and tags with zero network latency.
IndexedDB Architecture Jump to Chapter 1 →
Browser-native transactional database engine storing gigabytes of data privately on the client side without 5MB storage caps.
Modular Blueprint (5-Section Anatomy) Jump to Chapter 3 →
Enterprise prompt structure partitioning prompts into Persona, Objective, Dynamic Context Inputs, Negative Guardrails, and Output Rubric.
Multi-LLM Dispatcher Jump to Chapter 4 →
1-click launcher transferring pre-filled prompts directly to ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Cursor, or LibreChat.

Explicit anti-hallucination instructions specifying what the AI must NOT do (e.g. no conversational preamble, no speculative citations).
